hook: Whitworth arrived at privacy from communications law, FCC staff, telecom practice, online business counsel, before building a financial-sector privacy career that now spans one of the largest U.S. bank mergers. At Truist he oversees global privacy, technology compliance, and AI compliance across the full institution and its affiliates, making him an early practitioner of the combined privacy-AI governance function that regulators are now formalizing.
name: Ron Whitworth

quote.text: Ron Whitworth is Chief Privacy Officer at Truist in Charlotte, N.C., managing the Enterprise Privacy and Technology Office within Compliance Risk Management.

reading.body:
Ron Whitworth's career traces the path that financial-sector privacy governance now has to follow: from communications regulation through data law through AI compliance, all consolidated into a single institutional function at a top-ten U.S. bank.

His progression through FCC staff work, telecom practice, and online business counsel gave him a regulatory literacy that pure privacy specialists rarely acquire before entering financial services. That foundation became consequential when he moved into banking at EverBank, then carried the function through the SunTrust-BB&T merger into Truist, where the Enterprise Privacy and Technology Office now covers global privacy, technology compliance, and AI compliance together. Holding the scope of a combined institution across that full range is what makes the role structurally significant, not merely senior.

The data does not specify which AI systems Truist operates or what compute infrastructure underlies them. What it does show is that the compliance perimeter has been drawn to include AI explicitly, and that regulators are arriving at the same boundary independently, as his three appointed terms on the DHS Data Privacy and Integrity Advisory Committee suggest. Five IAPP certifications, including the AIGP, indicate that the combined privacy-AI governance function is now credentialed as a discipline, not improvised from adjacent fields.

quick_facts: Chief Privacy Officer at Truist Financial Corporation, managing the Enterprise Privacy and Technology Office (EPTO) for global privacy, technology, and AI compliance
Fellow of Information Privacy (FIP) and Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional (AIGP)
Holds five IAPP certifications: CIPP/US, CIPP/C, CIPP/E, CIPM, and AIGP
Appointed by the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security to the Data Privacy and Integrity Advisory Committee (DPIAC) in 2018; served three terms
Former attorney at Sullivan and Worcester LLP and Special Assistant to FCC Commissioner Jonathan Adelstein
